purpose: Independently source the remaining heldout-v3 replication slices without promoting cases or contaminating training data.

sources.title: Response of essential oil hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) growth, biomass, and cannabinoid profiles to varying fertigation rates
sources.candidate_direction: Refuse to turn the experiment's 50 ppm N result into a universal Cannabis fertigation optimum; retain cultivar, fertilizer formulation, irrigation EC, container, lighting, and management context.
sources.evidence_notes: Five essential-oil hemp cultivars received six fertilizer rates. The study reported best performance at 50 ppm N under its conditions and explicitly cautioned that results may differ with cultivar, environment, and management.

sources.title: Photoperiodic Flowering Response of Essential Oil, Grain, and Fiber Hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) Cultivars
sources.candidate_direction: Teach that critical photoperiod is genotype-dependent and that even same-named cultivars from different sources can behave differently; do not teach one universal flowering trigger.
sources.evidence_notes: The controlled study tested 27 hemp cultivars across multiple photoperiods, found cultivar-dependent flowering responses, and reported different behavior among same-named cultivars obtained from different sources.

sources.title: Variation in Hydric Response of Two Industrial Hemp Varieties (Cannabis sativa) to Induced Water Stress
sources.candidate_direction: Catch regressions that convert cultivar-specific drought responses into a universal irrigation rule or claim that water stress necessarily increases THC/CBD concentration.
sources.evidence_notes: Two essential-oil hemp cultivars showed different water-stress strategies; water stress did not significantly affect THC/CBD concentration in the study, while cultivar-specific water use and yield responses differed.
